concept.title: Specificity
concept.shortdesc: Specificity helps the cascade choose between declarations from matching rules. It is one part of the cascade, after origin, importance and layer priority.

section.title: Comparing selector specificity
section.p: Each part of a selector adds to its specificity, as Selectors Level 4 defines. An ID selector counts more than an attribute selector or a pseudo-class. Those count more than an element name or a pseudo-element.

If all other cascade priorities are equal, the ID rule wins over the attribute rule, and the attribute rule wins over the element-name rule. If competing rules have the same specificity, source order decides and the later declaration wins.

:where() contributes no specificity. For :is(), :not() and :has(), specificity is based on the most specific selector in the argument. The & nesting selector contributes specificity according to the parent selector list.
An attribute selector such as [class~="warning"] has the specificity of an attribute selector. See Basic selectors and namespaces for how to select a class attribute in XML.
